cues.text: A family from far away
Zlatan Ibrahimović was born in 1981 in Malmö, Sweden.
His father was a Bosniak, and his mother was a Croat.
Both had moved to Sweden, where they met.
Zlatan grew up in Rosengård, a part of Malmö where many families had come from other countries.
At six, he got a pair of football boots and began to play.
Open the club door.
One of his first clubs, FBK Balkan, was started by people who had moved from Yugoslavia.
Coming from more than one place is not a problem. Your family’s story is part of what makes you, you.
Running home for dinner
Zlatan’s parents were divorced, and his mum had five children to look after.
When he was nine, Zlatan went to live with his father.
There often was not much food at his dad’s home, and Zlatan often went hungry.
Run along the path to Mum’s.
When he was hungry, Zlatan would run to his mum’s home for dinner.
Many children would find that very hard.
When home is hard, it is never a child’s fault.
If home feels hard, tell a teacher or a grown-up you trust. You deserve help and care.
The wrong clothes
When Zlatan played with children from richer families, he felt he did not fit in, because he had the wrong clothes and no money.
His co-author, David Lagercrantz, wrote that Zlatan told himself: one day I’ll show them!
Flip the card.
That feeling became his motivation.
As a boy, he also went to taekwondo classes at a Malmö club called Enighet, which means unity.
His football hero was the Brazilian striker Ronaldo.
You do not need expensive things to belong. Being different can be a strength.
Almost giving up
In his early teens, Zlatan played for his hometown club, Malmö FF.
But at fifteen, he nearly gave up football.
He thought about taking a job at the Port of Malmö, where the big ships come in.
Open the gate back to the pitch.
His manager convinced him to keep playing.
Zlatan stayed, and in 1999 he moved up to Malmö’s first team.
In 2001, he joined Ajax in the Netherlands.
When you feel like giving up, talk to someone who believes in you. They may see what you cannot see yet.
A pitch for the next kids
In late 2007, Zlatan paid for a new football pitch in the streets of Rosengård, with help from a sports company.
It was called Zlatan Court.
It had a playing mat, goalposts, lights and a new fence.
Switch on the lights.
The next year, he gave new kits to his old youth club, FBK Balkan.
The boy who had once felt left out made sure that the children after him had a good place to play.
Remember where you came from, and help the children who come after you.
Back at thirty-six
On 20 April 2017, playing for Manchester United, Zlatan badly hurt the ligaments in his right knee.
It was a very serious injury, and he was thirty-five.
He worked hard to recover, and he came back on 18 November 2017.
Unfold the bridge back.
He kept playing for years.
At thirty-nine, he became the oldest player from outside Italy to score in Serie A, and at forty, he won the Italian league with AC Milan.
A setback is not the end of the story. Rest, work hard, and come back step by step.
